about: Copy of the entries of https://github.com/danbri/glitchcan-minigam/blob/master/magpie/cwplans/data-register.json for the files in this folder (paths relative to cwplans/). That file is the authority; this copy is written by tools/check-data-register.mjs --write in the main repository. Each file keeps the licence of its source; there is no blanket licence.

policy.personal_org_address_data: Restrictions suspended for this project during scoping, planning and prototyping (owner, October 2026; CLAUDE.md, Data ethics, exception).
policy.licence_limit: Never fetch or commit proprietary, restricted-licence or virally licensed data.
policy.crawls: Website crawls, direct and via the Internet Archive or Common Crawl, are fair use for scoping (owner, 2026-10-03). Each crawl-derived file names its method and date here. Re-check before anything leaves the prototyping phase.
policy.knowledge_graph: Owner, 2026-10-03: selected sources will later go through a data integration pipeline into a knowledge graph. So every source keeps a stable key here (with licence, URL and fetch date), every transform is an activity in pipeline.json (what it used, what it generated, its rules), and identifiers are kept as they come from the source (OSM ids, Wikidata QIDs, UPRNs, TOIDs, FHRS ids, company numbers, cwb- ids) so they can become IRIs. tools/check-data-register.mjs --write exports pipeline.jsonld (PROV-O, DCAT, Dublin Core).
policy.odbl: OpenStreetMap data (ODbL 1.0, share-alike) is allowed for now (owner, 2026-10-03). Its use is to be reviewed in full during planning and prototyping. Every committed file that holds OSM data, or data derived from it, is listed here with osm.use other than 'none'.

osm_use_values.raw: OSM elements as downloaded (tags and geometry)
osm_use_values.derived: a database built from OSM data together with other sources (geometry, names, tags)
osm_use_values.counts: only counts or short lists (street names, kinds) computed from OSM
osm_use_values.ids: only OSM element ids, as links or join keys
osm_use_values.notes: documentation that quotes or tabulates OSM-derived values
